title: Grab - Current Experience
subtitle: Grab food delivery, Vietnam · iPhone · app v33437965 · English interface

findings.where: Service grid, tab bar badges, floating bus button
findings.sees: About ten service icons in two rows (labels cut at the right edge), two ad cards, red dots and a “5” badge on three tabs, and a floating bus button over an ad.

findings.t: Navigation changes inside the food section
findings.where: Top banner, bottom tab bar, section titles
findings.sees: A promo banner fills the top third. Tabs change from Home, Moments, Payment, Activity, Messages to Discover, Near Me, Offers, Order Again, Cart (no Home). Near Me is both a tile and a tab. The same carousel is “Order Now” on Home and “Buy Now” here.

findings.where: Search field
findings.sees: The placeholder is “Search food” on Home and “What shall we deliver?” in the food section.

findings.t: Delivery address is small and ambiguous
findings.where: “Deliver now / Home” label; “Current location / Home” row
findings.sees: Address and time sit in the smallest text at the top. In the address screen “Current location” carries the sub-label “Home”, so GPS or saved address is unclear. The ⋮ menu has no label. The keyboard covers most of the list.

findings.t: Filter chip is unclear and clipped
findings.where: Filter chip row under the search
findings.sees: “Under 18.000đ” has a scooter icon but no label saying it is the delivery fee. The row is clipped on the right, so the last chip cannot be read.

findings.where: Voucher chip and restaurant names
findings.sees: “Min. spend 100.00…” is cut off, so the amount cannot be read. Restaurant names are cut too.

findings.where: Small “Ad” tag; “Showing results in Delivery” dropdown
findings.sees: The first two results for “Matcha” are both ads. The tag is small and grey. The search scope is a plain text dropdown.

findings.where: Fee line “Free 10.000đ” with the orange GrabUnlimited icon
findings.sees: Delivery is shown as free. At checkout the same order has “Delivery and applicable fees 17.000”. The page also offers “Join GrabUnlimited”, which suggests free is the member price. To confirm: is the account a member?

findings.where: Red pill at the bottom of the menu
findings.sees: The pill sits over the “For You” title, over a dish name, and over the “+” button of a dish.

findings.t: Menu starts with promos; categories hidden
findings.where: Chips and promo cards under the header; “Today’s Offer” dropdown
findings.sees: Before any menu item: Group Order, Order for Later, Menu language (cut off), three promo cards, Your Last Order, Today’s Offer, For You. Categories hide in one dropdown instead of tabs.

findings.where: Option groups, checkboxes and tags
findings.sees: “Optional, max 1” uses checkboxes, not radio buttons. Once one is ticked the others turn pale grey, so a change needs an untick first. The size group says “Optional” but “Ly 500ml” is already ticked. Group names are Vietnamese in an English screen.

findings.t: AI-generated text is easy to miss
findings.where: Grey italic line under the description
findings.sees: “Thông tin sản phẩm này được tạo bởi AI.” (the product text was made by AI) is small, pale and only in Vietnamese.

findings.where: Basket bar; fee lines on the order summary
findings.sees: The basket shows 47.000đ. The next screen adds delivery and applicable fees 17.000 and a small order fee 3.000, so the total is 67.000đ, about 42% more. Neither the reason nor the threshold of the small order fee is shown before.

findings.where: Red “See more options” button; banner under the fees
findings.sees: A large “Two restaurants, one delivery fee” block with a dark red button sits between the fees and the green “Place order”. A GrabUnlimited banner follows. Items, promotions, fees and savings share one long screen.

findings.where: Option cards, “VIP upgrade (12 remaining)”, (i) icons
findings.sees: Priority (17 mins) and Standard (24 mins) both cost 12.000, and Standard is pre-selected. “12 remaining” does not say 12 of what. “On-Time Promise” is not explained. The (i) icons are small. “Order for later” looks like a speed option but has no time or price.

findings.where: “Use offers and more” row; GrabCoins toggle
findings.sees: The row leading to vouchers and the code field says “Save VND3.000 using points”. The GrabCoins toggle is half hidden behind the sticky total bar.

findings.t: Expired card message has no fix
findings.where: Grey box at the top; grey radio in the linked list
findings.sees: “Your linked card has expired. Visit Help Centre” does not say which card, and the only action leaves the payment step. The expired card shows only as a grey, unselectable radio. To test: can it still be the default?

findings.t: Default payment is a hidden swipe
findings.where: “Swipe left to set your default”; Linked Methods list
findings.sees: Setting a default is an invisible swipe while the list already has radio buttons. It is unclear what a radio tap does (this order or the default). Cash and MoMo sit under “Linked Methods”.

findings.where: Grey paragraph under “saved securely”
findings.sees: “Your card may be charged to make sure it’s valid” is small grey text and does not say how much. The reassurance comes first, the money line second.

findings.where: Offers list; code field at the top
findings.sees: 8 of the 10 rows visible are greyed out (“Spend 172.500đ more” on a 46.500đ order). “Enter promo or gift code here” looks like search (magnifier). “Use GrabGifts” repeats it right below.

findings.t: Countdown sheet covers the tracking screen
findings.where: Red bottom sheet “GrabMore and save on delivery”
findings.sees: It covers the lower part of every tracking screen. The timer runs in real time (19:53 at 15:55, 12:42 at 16:02, 03:20 at 16:11), cuts the order total, and has no visible close button.

findings.where: “Check this out while you wait” card
findings.sees: Hotel membership ads (Modern Village, IHG) sit between the status and the order or driver details. They have nothing to do with the food order and hide behind a small ⋮.

findings.where: Bar under the ETA
findings.sees: Four icons (G, pot, scooter, house) and no text. Progress is shown only by green fill, so meaning rests on icon and colour.

The window stays unchanged from “We’ve got your order” to “Your order’s ready for delivery”. It becomes a point time (“Arriving by 4:17 PM”) only on the map. The app uses 12-hour time while the phone clock is 24-hour.

findings.where: Order card under the status
findings.sees: The order shows only as one thumbnail with a “View order summary” link. A Favourites prompt and an “Offers” row sit inside the card of an order already placed. What “Offers” can do now is unclear.

findings.t: Map does not frame driver and address
findings.where: Map edges; “GF-091” tag; address bubble
findings.sees: The driver icon is cut by the left edge and the address bubble (“[address hidden]”) by the right edge. “GF-091” has no label. Many shop names clutter the map.

findings.t: Tip card repeats; tap result unclear
findings.where: Tip card
findings.sees: The same tip card (5.000đ, 10.000đ, 20.000đ, Custom) shows three times, even before a driver is assigned. “Custom” is cut off. It is not visible whether a tap charges now or asks first. Provisional: test it.

findings.where: “Get help”; headset icon; “Contact driver” link; “Chat with merchant” and “Contact Grab”
findings.sees: Four labels in three places: blue “Get help” (J3 · 01 to 06), a headset icon plus a small “Contact driver” link (J3 · 07), and two buttons (J3 · 11). No screen offers a direct “report a problem” or refund route.

findings.where: Video block; feedback chips; “Submit”
findings.sees: Rating, feedback chips (“Attitu…” cut off), tip and Submit share one long screen, and a large video ad fills the lower half of J3 · 07. “GrabCoins +0” is unexplained. Submit does not show whether a tip is included.

findings.where: Blue links; Booking ID; fee line
findings.sees: “Rate order”, “Reorder”, “View details” are small blue links. “Rate order” is still shown at 16:14, the same minute as the rating, with no confirmation seen. “Booking ID” and “GF-091” are internal codes. “Applicable fees 20.000” merges the two checkout fees. “Profile: Personal” is not explained.
